#1035. Man City boss Enzo Maresca says Erling Haaland had goal wrongly disallowed

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The prolific Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno’s hands

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Enzo Maresca had no doubt Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal in Manchester City’s 1-1 draw with Fulham on Saturday should have stood.

The prolific Norwegian had an effort chalked off in the Premier League encounter at the Etihad Stadium when he was deemed to have kicked the ball out of Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno’s hands.

Haaland had not connected cleanly with a volley but Leno spilled the ball attempting to gather his attempt and the striker prodded in from close range.

Referee Thomas Bramall, however, ruled that Leno – because the ball was still between his hands – had not lost control and VAR Sam Barrott upheld the decision.

Maresca said: “I reviewed the goal after the game. From my point of view, it’s quite clear that it’s not a foul, but I’m not the guy that decides, unfortunately.”

Asked how Haaland viewed the incident, Maresca added: “When they were reviewing the VAR, he was absolutely sure that it was a goal, because I asked him from the touchline. He was completely sure that it was a goal but the referee decided for different things.”

With that effort ruled out in the 25th minute, City had to wait until just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener.

Elliot Anderson scored their equaliser with a fine volley – a sweet moment for the midfielder after being sent off playing for England last weekend.

Maresca said: “It was a nice moment for him, a nice moment for us because it gave us the chance to come back in the game.

“We used him today for the first time as an attacking midfielder. He was playing a little bit more deep with us. We are trying to find different solutions, the right balance, and to be more consistent.”

Anderson’s equaliser ended City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but it was nevertheless another frustrating result for a side that opened the campaign with seven straight wins.

Maresca said: “For sure we don’t like this kind of moments, in terms of four games in a row without a win.

“But we also know that, unfortunately, it’s normal or it’s part of your path that you go through these kind of moments.

“It’s important that we find a way to keep a clean sheet. Sometimes you need to win games 1-0.”

For Fulham, the result ended a sequence of 20 successive losses to City in all competitions and extended their unbeaten run to five games.

Manager Alvaro Arbeloa said: “We came here trying to win this match.

“Obviously we knew that we had lost the last 20 times against Man City, but I told them that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage, with character, if we press them so high, play the way we like to play.

“I think we played really, really well. We could have won the game, but for me the most important thing was the performance and the character of my team.”

#1034. Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return

Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated."

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward."

Shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS said that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence."

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

Two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there."

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship."

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically."

The spokesperson also said  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany."

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen said in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said.

This came shortly after Norway said it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

"Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation said it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia."

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

At the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

"We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker said.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had said it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear company Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

This article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.

#1033. Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds

There are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

“I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible plan or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

It is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

Noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ

“I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, said. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”

John Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

Frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a new star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett

What a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

It’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

What was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

Can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

This has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

1999 was the last time Leeds won at Chelsea. Today looks like they will get another, as Okafor takes advantage of more poor defending to finish past Martinez.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

They are getting their wish, too, as the Scotland international is coming on with winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Morgan Rogers and Chelsea are pretty upset about that penalty being awarded to Leeds. They felt the ball struck him too far up his arm to be a penalty. Calvert-Lewin took his spot-kick superbly and it’s gone very, very quiet among the home fans.

Everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

From almost the halfway line, he drove forward, weaving his way expertly into the box before picking out Dominic Solanke in the middle of the box, who tapped the ball into the back of the net.

However, the atmosphere is still a touch subdued, despite James Maddison urging the crowd to make themselves heard almost immediately after the goal, the noise drops to almost a murmur.

Rogers blocks Bogle’s drive with his arm and Michael Oliver gives a penalty to Leeds. After a long check, VAR confirms it.

Calvert-Lewin steps up and sends Martinez the wrong way. The away team deserves this. They have been the better side. That is Calvert-Lewin’s 100th club career goal.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

A real lack of quality here from both teams, and Sunderland deserve credit for weathering the early pressure.

Villa appear short of creativity and have managed only one shot on target in the first-half.

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Some boos from the Chelsea fans at half-time. Calvert-Lewin could have had a hat-trick in that first half, sending one header against the bar, two too close to Martinez and flicking a shot just wide. Leeds also had a goal ruled out for offside.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

That half was all about Luca Williams-Barnett. The 18-year-old scored in his first start, and had two opportunities to add to his tally just before the break. He had a header tipped over the bar by Christian Walton and a chance from close range stopped on the line. The future looks bright, as they say.

However, Tottenham faded after a strong opening 15 minutes, and Ipswich were able to break up play and get forward more, exploiting the home side’s lack of a defensive midfielder, and that will be something for Roberto De Zerbi to address in the break.

We have whistles around the ground. That was breathless stuff.

The visitors will feel they should be in front at the break. First, Muharemovic thinks he has scored when he head in a cross from Justin but he was offside.

Then Ampadu’s long throw finds Calvert-Lewin in space and his shot is saved by Martinez. Should have done better there.

Bournemouth finish the half in style. Kluivert gets the second when he taps in a cross from Tavernier.

Palace hit back again. Pino clips a cross to Larsen at the far post and he heads past Rushworth coolly.

Courtesy of Opta: Aged 18 years and 51 days, Luca Williams-Barnett is Tottenham Hotspur’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

Villa are in desperate need of a spark and one has to wonder when John McGinn will be introduced. McGinn is on the bench today and the home team are crying out for some inspiration.

Villa did start brilliantly, yet the game has now petered out into a mess of misplaced passes and poor decision-making.

Still no clean sheet for Emi Martinez. But Noah Okafor’s goal wasn’t his fault – he was let down by some bad defending from Wesley Fofana and Josh Acheampong.

Martinez did start Chelsea’s 2-0 victory over Everton, but he didn’t last the full game as he had to be replaced because of injury.

A touch of Hollywood royalty in attendance at Tottenham on this cold November afternoon with Sir Kenneth Branagh and Ryan Reynolds in attendance.

Reynolds is a co-owner of Wrexham, who are currently playing in the Championship at Lincoln City, but he has chosen to watch football in north London instead.

Sakamoto puts Palace back in front with a brilliant finish. Rudoni gets away from Khalaili and crosses to the Japan international. Sakamoto brings it down nicely then rifles a shot into the top corner.

That lead did not last long for Chelsea. The away side hit back within three minutes as Okafor shoots through the legs of Colwill and into the net.

Another full debutant and another goal. This time at Stamford Bridge as Emegha latches onto a ball from Rogers and blasts an unstoppable shot from distance.

Emegha had to wait a while to make his first start for Chelsea, but he’s marked it with a really well taken goal. Leeds will be disappointed with the time and space he and Morgan Rogers, who provided the assist, were given, but it was a good finish.

Caicedo just can’t get going this season. That back injury that forced him off the pitch for a minute earlier has now resulted in him having to be replaced by Jordan Henderson. That’s a real blow to Alonso and Chelsea.

Villa were completely dominant in the opening ten minutes but Sunderland have now managed to subdue the home team.

Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson are both impressing for the home team. Villa do appear a little vulnerable in defence when Sunderland do break forward.

Today will be a day that 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett will not forget in a hurry, he has been energetic since the start and marked his maiden Premier League start with an early goal.

The actual goal might have been a tap-in, but it has injected life into the crowd who had otherwise been largely subdued from the start.

Confusion on the touchline for Chelsea. Caicedo was down after hurting his back. Alonso tried to stop his phyisos going straight on to the pitch, but referee Michael Oliver called them on. That meant Caicedo had to spend a minute off the pitch under the latest rules.

Remember this moment because on his first senior start Williams-Barnet has made it a special one with goal. It was scrappy but he will not care. The Tottenham fans have been talking about his young fan for a long time.

Equaliser for Palace and Frank. Very good response from his players as Larsen flicks the ball to Pino and the Spain international fires into the net.

No shots on target from either side but it is already shaping up to be attack vs defence. Villa are dominating the goal and looking threatening.

Awoniyi is through one-on-one with Henderson, goes around the keeper but Disasi does brilliantly to recover and make the block.

Worst possible start for Frank and Palace as Awoniyi gets his second goal of the season with a cool finish.

A video of De Zerbi saying “let’s go” in a manner that might be more at home in American Football is shown before the teams come out onto the pitch.

The atmosphere feels a bit subdued so far, but it is an important match for Tottenham.

This is probably the kiss of death from me, but I’m really looking forward to watching Tarik Muharemovic today. The defender has impressed me every time I’ve watched Leeds on television this season and looks to be one of the signings of the summer. Dare I say it, but Chelsea could have done worse than sign him given their troubles at the back. Emi Martinez is back in goal for the home side. He’s yet to keep a clean sheet since signing from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa: Suzuki, Wan-Bissaka, Harwood-Bellis, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Goretzka, Alysson, Manzambi, Buendia, Jackson.Subs: Bizot, Mings, Barkley, McGinn, Mbaye, Joao Gomes, Madjo, Cisse, Hemmings.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

Construction news: work on the North Stand behind one of the Villa Park goals continues to progress.

There are clear structural changes since Villa’s last home game and a mural of fans makes it more appealing to look at.

This stand is scheduled to be ready for next season and will increase Villa’s capacity to over 50,000.

Tottenham’s impressive run of form came to a crashing halt with a 1-0 defeat to Leeds just before the international break, but manager Roberto De Zerbi will be hoping for a fresh start - even if he will not be pitchside after picking up a second yellow card of the season.

De Zerbi made six changes from the aforementioned defeat to Leeds, including a first start for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett, a player who has come through the club’s academy.

There is no place in the squad for Sandro Tonali or Tosin Adarabioyo, but James Maddison will start for the first time since the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea in October.

Aston Villa 2.0 was always likely to be a slow-burner, and it is proving exactly that for Unai Emery.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

There is no Alejandro Garnacho or Tammy Abraham in the matchday squad today.

Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

#1032. Mikel Arteta provides David Raya injury update: ‘Never good news’

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Noni Madueke rescued a point for the champions in a 2-2 draw at Newcastle but Raya was forced off injured

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Mikel Arteta said that goalkeeper David Raya will undergo an MRI scan on his injured shoulder as the Gunners boss lamented his side dropping two points following a 2-2 draw at Newcastle.

Eberechi Eze put Arsenal ahead just past the half hour and he saw a free-kick saved on the stroke of half-time after Noni Madueke spurned a couple of chances to put the visitors further in front.

But Newcastle, booed off at the break, rallied on the resumption and Martin Odegaard being dispossessed from a throw-in allowed Harvey Barnes to score while Dan Burn’s free header from a corner caused a goalmouth scramble and Malick Thiaw capitalised to poke home from a yard out.

Arsenal then lost goalkeeper Raya to injury, although they claimed a share of the spoils thanks to Madueke 12 minutes from time as the Premier League leaders moved six points clear of Brighton, who could halve the deficit when they play at Hull on Sunday.

Arteta said: “My feeling is we have lost two points. We were exceptional in the first half from the beginning to the end. We should have been two, three or four-nil up clearly.

“When you don’t do that then the opponent is going to try to react and right from the beginning (of the second half) we weren’t at the races. One thing is to give them belief and another thing is to give them a goal. We did both.

“After that, we came back and we were exceptional. We scored the second goal and we had opportunities to go and kill the game. We lacked a moment of magic to be able to do that.

“It’s a pity because the margin should have been much bigger for the level we showed. I never remember that we played at that level here, never. We have won football matches playing much worse than we did today here.”

Raya was forced off in the 70th minute, having received treatment when he slumped to the floor after coming out to collect a corner, and left the field clutching his arm with an apparent shoulder problem.

Arteta said: “Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news. He will get assessed now and he will probably have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly because at the moment, I don’t know.”

Bruno Guimaraes also made way when Raya was withdrawn, with the former Newcastle midfielder’s every touch heavily barracked on his first return to Tyneside since his £75m move in the summer.

Arteta, though, spoke favourably of the Brazilian’s performance, adding: “It’s never easy, emotionally, you have so much going on, especially the way he feels connected to this club. But I thought he had a very good performance.”

Matthias Jaissle reflected on a performance of two halves – but Newcastle’s head coach hopes they can take their second 45-minute display into the rest of the season.

The German said: “It was pretty clear in the first half we were not that front-foot or that intense, somehow hesitating to make the last step or last yard.

“This is something you can’t afford against a top team. But the second half was pure belief, pure conviction, no hesitation any more, pure trust between the team-mates that they are doing their jobs.

“This is the Newcastle DNA and I hope we can build on the second half.”

#1030. Roberto De Zerbi compares Luca Williams-Barnett to Lamine Yamal after Tottenham win

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Williams-Barnett scored after 15 minutes and then set up Dominic Solanke

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.

De Zerbi turned to the highly-rated Spurs academy graduate after two bright cameos and he delivered with aplomb, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half.

After Williams-Barnett made his senior debut at the age of 16 last season, the clamour for the teenager to play has only increased during a difficult last 12 months and De Zerbi decided 10 days ago to include him in the starting line-up against Ipswich.

During a chat on Thursday with the skilful England Under-19 international, De Zerbi asked Williams-Barnett to play with freedom and work hard without the ball “like Raphinha, like Yamal” before he agreed when asked if the teenager could reach similar heights.

After De Zerbi revealed Williams-Barnett prepared for the match on the team bus by watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, he said: “Luca is a special player.

“I’m not surprised, because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. I think he’s lucky, because he’s playing in a top club, with top team-mates.

“I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was (James) Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

“The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

“And to play and to work hard without the ball, like (Ousmane) Dembele, like Raphinha, like Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

“Even if they are Ballon d’Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.”

Asked if Williams-Barnett can reach the level of Yamal, De Zerbi said: “Yes, I think so.

“And one of the best things in my career… I’ve seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

“I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?”

Gary O’Neil watched Ipswich’s winless run extend to five matches.

“Many of us weren’t quite able to get to the level that we’re used to. A tough afternoon. I didn’t enjoy it but I did enjoy watching the lads dig in and find a way to keep going together in a tough moment because that’s what we need,” O’Neil said.

“Between the goals and after the goals, we were OK and we arrived in the final third enough to cause problems but we didn’t. Disappointing but it was a big task coming here and we needed things to be perfect.”

The Brazilian winger had his pick of Premier League clubs when he left Russia in 2013

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Brazilian winger Willian enjoyed a successful career in English football, turning out more than 400 times for Chelsea, Arsenal and Fulham,

During this time, he established himself as one of the Premier League’s most exciting attackers, most notably at Stamford Bridge, where he won two league titles, an FA Cup, a League Cup and the Europa League.

But this move to the Blues in 2013 almost didn’t happen, as the Brazilian had a host of options when he chose to leave Russian side Anzhi Makhachkala.

After enjoying success at Shakhtar Donetsk, where he won five Ukrainian Premier League titles in a six-season spell, Willian was snapped up by the ambitious Anzhi.

“I wanted a new challenge [after Shakhtar] and Anzhi had very big ambitions. As well as Eto’o, Lassana Diarra was also there,” the Brazilian tells FourFourTwo.

But when the club’s ailing owner withdrew his financial backing, the project faced an uncertain future.

“But I ended up staying for only six months as, unfortunately, the owner had some health problems and decided he wouldn't invest in the club any more. So he sold all the players he had invested in, and that's why I left.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Using London as a base, Willian began negotiations with a host of clubs as he looked to resolve his future.

“When I left Russia, I stayed in London for about two weeks and negotiated with Spurs – but not only them,” he adds. “Liverpool were also in talks.

But while Spurs pushed especially hard to sign the former Corinthians youngster, Willian had his heart set elsewhere.

“But in my heart, I always had this desire to play for Chelsea,” he admits. “Anyway, they didn’t make a move and everything was practically settled with Tottenham.

“Then, on the day I was supposed to sign, I got a call from Chelsea director Marina Granovskaia, saying they wanted me. I immediately told her, ‘I want to join Chelsea’. They made an offer and it worked out.

“It was a dream to play there and thank god it happened.”

Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

#1028. Moises Caicedo forced off in tears as Chelsea injury crisis worsens

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Chelsea will be sweating over the fitness of their midfield lynchpin after his latest setback

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Moises Caicedo was forced off in the first half of Chelsea’s thrashing by Leeds as Xabi Alonso’s injury problems continue to mount.

The Ecuadorian lynchpin suffered a bad landing after meeting James Justin’s aerial challenge, which saw him twist in midair and land on his tailbone.

Caicedo was initially able to continue but after being troubled by his back in the following minutes, repeatedly holding the problem area, he went down off the ball, covering his seemingly tearful eyes with his shirt in dejection.

He was replaced by Jordan Henderson in the 22nd minute, but did not go straight down the tunnel for further treatment, instead taking a seat on the bench with an ice pack.

Alonso said after the 4-1 defeat that Caicedo had picked up a “knock” and that Chelsea would have to wait and see following further assessments on Sunday.

“He was in pain and let's see how bad it is,” Alonso said.

The circumstances in which Caicedo’s injury was dealt with left the Chelsea dugout unhappy with referee Michael Oliver.

Caicedo agonised on the deck for a considerable period before the Blues eventually sent their medical team on to treat him, with club doctors delaying their entry onto the pitch to try and prevent him having to come off for a minute, as per a new rule introduced in the Premier League this season.

Seemingly for the same reason, Caicedo leapt up and refused treatment from Chelsea medics when they approached him, but Oliver still ordered him to the touchline, reducing Chelsea to 10 men for a minute.

Caicedo also suffered a fitness scare during the international break when he was replaced at half-time of Ecuador’s 2-0 friendly win over Bolivia in midweek after feeling unwell.

The Blues are already without a number of key members due to injury including Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro, with the club struggling for form following four defeats in five.

#1027. Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release

In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

On November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour."

The crowds showed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

At first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

But in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an issue Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

The "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

The eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO says, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently said she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

#1025. Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Max Kozlov is a senior reporter with Nature in Washington DC.

Researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr. Chris Henstridge/SPL

A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms. Now, neuroscientists are discovering that the brain is the conductor of these responses — decoding the type of pathogen that has invaded, accessing memories of past bouts of illness and even mobilizing immune defences at the sight of a sick person.

The findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell. Neuroscientists have long viewed neurological responses to infection as a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation, rather than a strategy tailored to the threat.

“Sickness is actually not a fixed program, although we often talk about it this way,” said Jessica Osterhout, a neurobiologist at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who chaired the session.

A bacterial infection and a cold caused by a virus can both result in fever and exhaustion, yet they rarely trigger the same constellation of symptoms. Bacterial infections, for instance, tend to suppress appetite much more sharply than do colds, which made Osterhout and her colleagues wonder how the brain tells various pathogens apart.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover

In unpublished experiments, Osterhout’s team compared mice injected with a bacterial toxin with those given a compound that mimics a viral infection. To see how the brain distinguished between pathogens, the researchers profiled individual cells in circumventricular organs, which are specialized structures with unusually permeable blood vessels that surround brain ventricles.

When the body has an infection, cells in the circumventricular organs switch on sets of immune-related genes and release distinct mixes of chemical signals. Those signals diffuse to nearby neurons and create distinct patterns of activity for different pathogens, allowing the brain to customize its symptom profile depending on the threat.

Rather than acting as conduits that let inflammatory signals pass unchecked from the blood into the wider brain, these structures “may actually interpret them”, Osterhout said.

Sometimes, the brain doesn’t even wait for pathogens to enter the body to rally the immune system1. Andrea Serino, a neuroscientist at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, studies how the brain maps peripersonal space, which is the area around the body roughly in arm’s reach.

When Serino’s team placed volunteers in virtual reality, they found that threat-monitoring brain regions became active when avatars bearing skin lesions caused by viral or bacterial infections approached, even when the figures were beyond arm’s reach. Just 15 minutes of virtual exposure triggered a surge in frontline immune ‘sentinel’ cells in participants’ blood comparable to that induced by an influenza vaccine. This reaction did not occur when participants saw healthy-looking avatars or ones expressing fear.

These experiments suggest that the immune system uses “the predictive ability of the brain to react before pathogens enter the body”, Serino said.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03774-w

#1024. Noni Madueke rescues Arsenal and salvages point against inspired Newcastle

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Eberechi Eze sent the Gunners ahead before goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw changed the momentum after the break

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Noni Madueke snatched a 2-2 draw for Arsenal after Newcastle produced a stunning second-half turnaround to claim a deserved point against the Premier League leaders.

Eberechi Eze put the champions in front and Madueke wasted a couple of chances to increase the lead before half-time, with Matthias Jaissle’s side jeered off following a listless first 45 minutes.

They rallied in stunning fashion on the resumption, with Harvey Barnes scoring Newcastle’s first goal at St James’ Park since September 19 before Malick Thiaw put them ahead after the hour from close range.

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes underwhelmed on his return to Tyneside, his every touch booed before he was brought off after 70 minutes, but his new employers claimed a share of the spoils thanks to Madueke.

Arsenal’s five-match winning run in the league was halted, although they extended their lead at the top of the table to six points over second-placed Brighton, who could halve the deficit at Hull on Sunday.

Newcastle came into the fixture with significant concerns about where their goals were coming from and they were up against the most miserly defence in the league, with Arsenal conceding just five times in their previous 10 games.

Newcastle were given an early warning when Madueke cut inside and left England team-mate Dan Burn trailing in his wake, with the Arsenal forward’s low shot to the near post hitting the outside of it.

Arsenal’s press meant there was no let-up for Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who made a series of distribution errors, and it was a heart-in-mouth moment for the home side’s fans when Guimaraes got ahead of Barnes but the Brazilian could not direct a sliding volley on-target.

The Magpies’ luck ran out in the 33rd minute when Kai Havertz dispossessed Lewis Hall before sliding a perfectly-weighted pass to Eze, who went in behind Amar Dedic to finish coolly past Hornicek.

Matters might have worsened before half-time as more loose play allowed Madueke to pick his pocket. Madueke bore down on goal but took one touch too many before his shot was saved by Hornicek.

Hall made partial amends to then deny Madueke’s shot while Eze’s free-kick was saved as Arsenal ended the half on top, prompting Jaissle to make a triple substitution at the break, with Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Tino Livramento replacing Jacob Murphy and Dedic and Sean Steur.

Newcastle exploded out of the traps and needed just four minutes after the restart to draw level, with Martin Odegaard nudged off the ball by Joe Willock and the ball dropping to William Osula, who teed up Barnes to fire beyond David Raya with aplomb.

It was Newcastle’s first goal at home in 312 minutes and with the crowd now firmly behind them, they remarkably took the lead with Arsenal at sixes and sevens.

The unmarked Burn headed Hall’s corner on-target and a goalmouth scramble between Willock and Arsenal duo Gabriel and Raya led to Thiaw poking home from a yard out in the 62nd minute.

Arteta was forced into a substitution with Raya suffering a shoulder injury, while Guimaraes was also hooked alongside Eze with 20 minutes to go to the delight of Newcastle’s supporters as Kepa Arrizabalaga, Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly were introduced.

Newcastle continued to pile forward but were undone in the 78th minute when a fluid move forwards from Arsenal ended with Madueke cutting onto his left foot and dispatching through Hornicek’s hands and in.

Both sides had chances to claim victory in a frenzied atmosphere but neither could manage another breakthrough before Guimaraes, the first Newcastle captain to lift a trophy in 56 years following their historic 2025 Carabao Cup triumph, was cheered at full-time when he completed a lap of the pitch.

#1023. Whiff of arrogance as Arsenal unexpectedly implode

Arsenal were cruising. This was life on Premier League easy street, but from complete control of this game against Newcastle United, they tossed it away. It was a spectacular, unexpected implosion. They were extremely fortunate to escape with a point.

You cannot switch off away from home in the Premier League and you certainly can never be complacent against a team with Newcastle’s home crowd behind them.

From control to disarray. From looking like champions, Arsenal, who also lost goalkeeper David Raya to a worrying looking injury, rumbled under pressure. To go from dominance to being grateful for a draw, this was a flaky side of the Premier League leaders we have not seen for a while.

“We have lost two points,” said manager Mikel Arteta. “We were exceptional in the first half, the intensity and the quality, we should have been two, three or four goals up.

“When you don’t do that, in the second half you cannot give the opposition belief and you cannot give them goals. We did both. We started to lose duels, second balls, we gave it away.”

Was it arrogance? Did the title-holders start to believe they were simply too good to be hurt or worried by a team with Newcastle’s obvious limitations? It looked like it. The way Arsenal fell apart as soon as the momentum in the game shifted in the home team’s favour in the second half was shocking.

Newcastle were dreadful before the break and managed just one attack before half-time. Perhaps it was all too easy for Arteta’s side. They have become used to ferocious battles on Tyneside, but this was a stroll for 45 minutes. When it turned into a proper test after half-time, though, they folded.

"Absolutely clinical!" Eberechi Eze scores his first Premier League goal of the season to give Arsenal the lead 🔴 https://t.co/34IbZuuJuN

The visitors took a deserved lead, through Eberechi Eze, having barely had to break sweat, but the way they approached the second half was baffling. As soon as Newcastle got in their faces and made it a scrap, Arsenal were bullied, ruffled and rushed into mistakes.

To give the opposition one goal against the run of play can be forgiven, but to do it a second time, when the heat is cranked up, hints at a fragility we no longer thought existed under Arteta.

The first goal came from a blunder by captain Martin Odegaard. It was a lazy, sloppy swing of the leg to try to clear a throw-in and the ball sliced backwards. When it looped into the path of Will Osula, he squared to the unmarked Harvey Barnes who put away the equaliser comfortably.

"Horrendous error!" Harvey Barnes puts Newcastle level 👊 https://t.co/YWrHZPxBIo

It was Newcastle’s first shot on target, but Arsenal’s air of invincibility vanished and the crowd sensed it. Newcastle players responded to the noise, snapping into tackles and pouring forward in numbers, yet the second goal was also an Arsenal gift.

How do you leave the giant Dan Burn unmarked at a corner? Newcastle’s captain had so much time and space the crowd were able to scream in anticipation before his header flew goalwards, eventually bundled across the line by his centre-back colleague Malick Thiaw.

Malick Thiaw is in the right place to fire it in and give Newcastle the lead against Arsenal! 🔥 https://t.co/nthaH3aOJD

Newcastle deserved it. For half an hour in the second half they were the better side. From the depths of despair, from the apathy and boos of half-time, this was a completely different team.

If this is the vertical football Matthias Jaissle has preached since he arrived in August, Newcastle supporters can buy into it. There was speed, a physicality and a boldness in this second-half performance. It was fun and exciting. It was football played on the front foot. It was what we were promised when the German replaced Eddie Howe.

“That is Newcastle’s DNA, the second half is what we want this team to play like,” said Jaissle. “We knew there would be ups and downs this season, but if we can put that performance together for 90 minutes we can definitely say we are moving in the right direction.”

The problem is, Newcastle have not put a 90-minute performance like this together all season. We have only seen it in flashes and as good as the second half was, we cannot lose sight of the fact the first was abject. Newcastle’s football was aimless, clueless and dysfunctional. One attack before the break, one deflected shot wide is simply not good enough.

The transformation at half-time was unexpected. The substitutes helped; Tino Livramento was a massive upgrade on Amar Dedic at right-back, Jacob Ramsey improved the midfield and Anthony Elanga brought speed and, yes, a vertical threat to their attack.

But Jaissle’s side did not hold on for the win. They had the chances to score a third, but it was their ambition to do so that caused their downfall. Arsenal’s class shone again, passing through the lines to release Noni Madueke.

The winger still had lots to do, but having cut inside, leaving two Newcastle defenders on the ground, his shot squeezed through a crowd and through the arms of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. The Czech international will not want to see it again, and this comes after a similar mistake in the home defeat to Everton.

Noni Madueke equalises for Arsenal! 💥 https://t.co/VNXOoNDxiJ

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

Jaissle has ordered a triple change, with Ramsey, Elanga and Livramento replacing Steur, Murphy and Dedic.

There’s a break in the play at the start of this half as Willock accidentally collides with Raya and the Arsenal goalkeeper holds his head. The medical staff are on to treat him.

Another abject, clueless, and directionless performance from Newcastle United in front of their own supporters. Arsenal have dominated the game and have not had to get out of second gear. It is hard to see what Matthias Jaissle’s team is trying to do and patience is wearing thin.

Yes, of course, they are playing the best team in the country but the supporters are not stupid. They have seen this sort of performance far too many times already this season. The most damning thing you can say is that there is no excitement. Even the boos for Bruno are half-hearted.

Boos ring out on the half-time whistle from the home fans. It’s been complete and utter domination from Arsenal. Eze’s resounding finish separates the sides, but the visitors could easily be two or three goals ahead. Newcastle look clueless in possession and are yet to record a shot on target.

Hall makes a goal-saving block! On this occasion, he comes to Newcastle’s rescue. Odegaard rolls a pass into the onrushing Madueke, who makes a great run drifting in from the right wing. Hall tracks the Arsenal attacker and makes a brilliant sliding block to deny Madueke from close range.

Once again, Hall switches off and Madueke pounces on the defender’s mistake as he tries to let the ball travel out of play. Madueke keeps it in and leads an Arsenal attack, but from a tight angle and under pressure from the covering Thiaw, his shot is smothered by Hornicek.

Arsenal are cruising and we’re still waiting for Newcastle to wake up. The away side haven’t created loads of chances, but they’re in control and have limited the hosts to nearly zero attacking threat.

After zero goals in his first ten matches for club and country this season, Eberechi Eze has now scored three goals in his last eight appearances.

All the noise inside St James’ Park is coming from the travelling Arsenal fans. Newcastle look lost and are really struggling to fashion any patterns of play in possession.

It’s a clinical opener for the visitors and Eze has his first Premier League goal of the season. Hall fails to deal with Konsa’s long ball and Havertz steals possession from him. The German then slides a delightful reverse pass behind Dedic and through to Eze, who lets the ball run across his body before smashing a clinical one-on-one effort into the roof of the net. Arsenal are deservedly ahead and Newcastle have barely laid a glove on them.

"Absolutely clinical!" Eberechi Eze scores his first Premier League goal of the season to give Arsenal the lead 🔴 https://t.co/34IbZuuJuN

St James’ Park was about to erupt, and not in a good way for the hosts! Rice clips such an inviting cross into the box and Guimaraes throws himself at the delivery, directing it narrowly wide of the bottom corner with an outstretched leg. The Newcastle fans behind the goal give the Brazilian some stick as he gets back to his feet.

Arsenal are dominating possession and territory. Newcastle United are struggling to advance up the pitch, and once again, there still seems to be no real improvement in Jaissle’s “vertical football” approach.

The theory following the German’s move from Saudi Arabia was that his team is better suited to playing against stronger opponents when there are more gaps to exploit in a side that constantly looks to attack.

We shall see about that. Other than a deflected Jacob Murphy shot from distance the home team has not had a meaningful attack yet.

Dedic picks up the game’s first yellow card after he pulls Eze back. The Newcastle right-back needs to be careful now.

After 23 minutes, Newcastle goalkeeper Lukás Hornícek has had 15 touches of the ball. Only Dan Burn and Lewis Hall have had more for Newcastle. The home side seem unable to work the ball forward at all. Seemingly every passage of possession results in a Newcastle player turning towards their own goal and shovelling it back to the keeper.

Safe to say that Hornicek does not look comfortable with the ball at his feet. Dedic passes back to him and under a little bit of pressure from Odegaard, he boots the ball straight out of play. From there, Arsenal fashion an attack as Timber strides forward and finds Havertz, who lashes a shot wide from a tight angle.

This game is yet to burst into life. It’s been a relatively measured start from both sides so far. Guimaraes has only had 12 touches so the boos have been limited to this point.

Murphy chops inside of Calafiori and smashes a shot at goal. It takes a massive deflection off Barnes, who was trying to get out of the way, but the ball flies just wide of Arsenal’s near post. Raya was worried for a second there as he frantically dived to make sure.

Hornicek is nearly embarrassed by Havertz as the Newcastle goalkeeper dawdles on the ball and takes too long to clear. The German forward closes in and blocks Hornicek’s kick, but luckily for the hosts, the ball spins away from goal towards Hall’s feet.

Arsenal go close early on. Eze drifts into a central position and brings down a long ball before teeing up Madueke, who dances inside of Burn and fires a powerful effort against the base of the woodwork. Hornicek seemed to have it covered at his near post, but that was still a notable opening for Arsenal.

Murphy does well to barge past Guimaraes and then attempts a very ambitious lob over Raya from just inside Arsenal’s half. However, the Newcastle man’s hopeful effort skids very far off target. It would take a miracle to beat Raya from that range.

More than £300m worth of signings are on the Newcastle bench this evening and another £72m sitting in the stands. That points to some bungled recruitment decisions over the last 18 months.

The fact that neither Aladji Bamba nor Bazoumane Toure can even make the matchday squad after joining in the summer before Matthias Jaissle was appointed manager is also damning.

There could be some awkward conversations between Jaissle and sporting director Ross Wilson before the January transfer window.

Then again, it was Jaissle who pushed to sign Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City and was thrilled to sign Mathias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille. They cost just over £100m and both only  make the bench against  Arsenal.

St James’ Park is absolutely bouncing. Can Newcastle upset Arsenal’s rhythm and disrupt the runaway leaders’ winning run?

Loud boos and whistles from Newcastle fans when Bruno Guimraes’ name is announced in the Arsenal team and a huge cheer from the away fans.

Manchester United inquired about signing Hall in the summer but were told that the 22-year-old was not for sale in that window.

They did not follow up on their initial approach and Hall signed a new long-term contract in September that has made him one of Newcastle’s top earners.

On their way to lifting the Premier League trophy title last season, Arsenal claimed a dramatic 2-1 victory over Newcastle at St James’ Park in September 2025, with Gabriel nodding in a 96th minute winner. Time will tell but I think it is a mistake by Mikel Arteta to have named Bruno Guimaraes in his starting XI against Newcastle United.

The Newcastle crowd has been subdued and occasionally angry this season given the limp displays under Matthias Jaissle but the presence of Bruno in the opposition team will unify the fanbase and whip up the crowd into an angry frenzy.

The champions, though, fear nobody and rightly so. They have looked the best team in the country so far this season and probably do not feel they have anything to worry about against a poor Newcastle side. We shall see.

Bruno Guimarães’s move to Arsenal was one of the most explosive transfers of the summer as Newcastle United’s talisman and captain left a club where he was adored.

As the Brazil international returns to St James’ Park on Saturday evening for the first time since completing his £75m switch in August, the circumstances around his controversial exit are brought back into focus.

Guimarães hurt a lot of people when he forced his way out and while the wounds will heal in time given how brilliant the midfielder was for 4½ years, he can expect a hostile reception.

The 29-year-old was a majestic player for Newcastle, but the way he conducted himself in the summer left supporters feeling betrayed. Telegraph Sport reveals for the first time the events leading up to his Arsenal move, what motivated it and what is behind his inconsistent start at the Emirates.

#1021. Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat said. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a big relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome."

Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed."

Growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," said Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

"I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

"I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat said. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a big change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships."

As well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat said.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she said. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself."

That has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

"The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she said.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride."

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.
